title: Termination without Cause, Notice Periods and Rescission — Network Participation Agreements Article
content:
**Article.** Either party may end an agreement under the **Network Participation Agreements** without cause by written notice. The practice gives the agreement type's provider notice period. Cascade gives the agreement type's carrier notice period.

## 1. Termination date

The notice period is the notice date plus the notice days, counted in calendar days. The termination date is the last day of the month in which the notice period ends.

There is one alternative for the practice. After a material fee schedule reduction, the practice may give the shorter material-change notice instead, if it gives notice within the fee schedule change notice window before the reduction takes effect.

| Agreement type | Practice's notice (days) | Cascade's notice (days) |
|---|---|---|
| Cascade Savings Network Participating Provider Agreement | 30 | 30 |
| Cascade Vision Network Provider Agreement | 60 | 60 |
| Cascade DHMO Specialist Agreement | 90 | 90 |
| Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement | 90 | 90 |
| Cascade Premier Participating Dentist Agreement | 90 | 90 |
| Cascade PPO Participating Dentist Agreement | 90 | 90 |

## 2. The practice's own notice and rescission

A practice's own termination notice or rescission is the practice's decision. It is registered by the agent as a practice request and carried out only after the practice confirms it.

A termination notice or rescission from the practice is carried out only once the practice's request for that agreement is confirmed.

The confirmation is read from Cascade's record of the practice request for that same agreement. The request must show the status "confirmed" before the notice or rescission is carried out.

## 3. Rescission

A practice may rescind its own notice while the agreement is termination pending and before the termination date. A notice given by Cascade can be withdrawn only by Cascade.

## 4. Network status through the termination date

The provider stays in network through the termination date. A member's service is in or out of network according to the agreement status on the date of service. For a multi-visit dental procedure, that date is the procedure start date. For an orthodontic case, it is the banding date.

Assigned DHMO members are reassigned the agreement type's reassignment lead time before a primary care dentist's termination date. Under the Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement, that lead time is 30 days.

## Worked example (hypothetical)

A primary care dentist gives written notice on 15 January under the Cascade DHMO Primary Care Dentist Agreement.

- The 90-day notice period ends on 15 April, so the termination date is 30 April.
- The dentist's assigned members are reassigned by 31 March, 30 days before that date.
- A crown started on 28 April is in network, even if the seat visit falls in May.
- If the dentist's confirmed request to rescind is carried out on 10 April, the agreement returns to active.
